comments.text:
I like where Nate is going with this, but I would suggest you spend more time on it. What you guys call discovery, we call workforce anthropology. 

Work has four categories: SOP, Human Talent, Heroics, and Duct-tape. If you automate the SOP without a full understanding of the other areas, heroics and duct-tape tasks will fill the 20 hours you just freed, and they will not feel the benefit of AI. 


Teo: Every company has a queue of ambitions and unmet needs. Ask them to write those on a whiteboard. Now you have a place to aim the saved hours. 

Spend more time asking questions and observing. And ask them: who do you say you are? Who they are will have a bigger impact on your long-term relationship than any AI automation

comments.text:
Yes, No-code + Web3 automation is absolutely doable. n8n, Make, or Moralis can link on-chain events (mints, transfers) to off-chain actions (emails, Sheets, Discord) in under 5 minutes.

But @ABUNDANCEandBEYONDATHLETE has a point buried in that laugh—that connection is just the surface. The real grind is baking Gas optimization, Private Key Vaulting, RPC Failover, and Contract ABI mapping into your no-code workflows.

Fewer than 1% globally can genuinely handle both domains (Automation + Blockchain Architecture) at a production-grade, scalable level. It takes deep architecture knowledge to move from a 'demo' to a truly 'deployed' system.

Your question cuts deeper than a simple yes/no—it asks how far you can push this and how safely you can pull it off.

So remember: everything is possible, and always expect the unexpected in this space. 💀🔥
